activeRecallQuiz.scenario: An investor holds 1,000 shares at $28 ($28,000 total) and buys 10 July Put contracts ($27.50 strike, 100 shares each) at $1.00 per option ($1,000 total cost). If the stock plunges to $20 in July, what is the investor's net portfolio value after subtracting the option cost?
activeRecallQuiz.question: An investor holds 1,000 shares at $28 ($28,000 total) and buys 10 July Put contracts ($27.50 strike, 100 shares each) at $1.00 per option ($1,000 total cost). If the stock plunges to $20 in July, what is the investor's net portfolio value after subtracting the option cost?
activeRecallQuiz.correctAnswer: Spot on! The 10 Put contracts give the investor the right to sell all 1,000 shares at the $27.50 strike price for $27,500 gross. Subtracting the $1,000 upfront option premium leaves a guaranteed net value of $26,500—saving $6,500 compared to an unhedged portfolio worth only $20,000!
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: Applying grounded principles prevents catastrophic losses and capital depletion.

coreTakeaways: Always evaluate underlying market assumptions before entering positions.

Follow disciplined risk and position sizing limits on every trade.
